concepts.heading: The RADAR Check-in System
concepts.plain: RADAR is a regular relationship check-in with a set order of steps.

concepts.heading: What RADAR Stands For
concepts.plain: It starts with a review of what has been happening since the last check-in.

concepts.heading: Why Structured Check-ins Matter
concepts.plain: Most of us were never taught to do upkeep talks. A set format makes it easier.

concepts.heading: Adapting RADAR for ENM
concepts.plain: With several partners, give each relationship its own check-in.

concepts.heading: Making It Feel Natural
concepts.plain: Keep it warm, not like a work meeting.

checks.prompt: What does the first R in RADAR stand for?
checks.explanation: Review. R is for Review: start by reviewing what has been happening since the last check-in.

options: Many people were never taught how to have maintenance conversations
checks.explanation: Many people were never taught how to have maintenance conversations. Many people were never taught how to have maintenance conversations about relationships.

a0539781-e2fc-469e-878e-808c32e418a2.takeaway: RADAR is a regular check-in with set steps, so small issues get talked about before they grow.

concepts.heading: Agreements vs Rules
concepts.plain: A rule and an agreement are different things, and the difference matters.

concepts.heading: The Core Distinction
concepts.plain: A rule is put on your partner. An agreement is something you both choose.

concepts.heading: Common Rules Worth Reexamining
concepts.plain: Some common rules, like the power to end a partner's other relationship, deserve a second look.

concepts.heading: Building Agreements
concepts.plain: Find the need underneath, like feeling secure, then agree on how to meet it.

concepts.heading: When Agreements Are Broken
concepts.plain: A broken agreement needs a different response from a broken rule. Talk about what happened.

options: Rules are imposed on a partner
checks.explanation: Rules are imposed on a partner. Rules are imposed on a partner. Agreements are created together.

options: The ability to end a partner's other relationship
checks.explanation: The ability to end a partner's other relationship. Veto power is the ability to end a partner's other relationship. The lesson says it deserves thoughtful reexamination.

f90739a6-3cd9-4829-83b3-ae6d5cbfd1ac.takeaway: Rules are put on a partner. Agreements are made together. Build agreements around the real need.

concepts.heading: Hierarchy, Non-Hierarchy, & Solo Poly
concepts.plain: How you set up your relationships is a big choice.

concepts.heading: Prescriptive vs Descriptive Hierarchy
concepts.plain: Some rankings are set in advance and limit what other relationships can become.

concepts.heading: Couple Privilege
concepts.plain: An existing couple has built-in advantages over newer partners. Notice them.

concepts.heading: Non-Hierarchical Polyamory
concepts.plain: Non-hierarchical means no relationship is capped in advance.

concepts.heading: Solo Polyamory
concepts.plain: Solo polyamory puts your own independence at the centre.

concepts.heading: Choosing Your Structure
concepts.plain: Research suggests no one structure is best for everyone.

options: The advantages established couples have over newer partners
checks.explanation: The advantages established couples have over newer partners. Couple privilege refers to the social, legal, and practical advantages that established couples have over newer or non-primary partners.

checks.prompt: What does Sheff's research suggest about structures?
options: No single structure is universally superior
checks.explanation: No single structure is universally superior. Dr. Elisabeth Sheff's longitudinal research on CNM families suggests that no single structure is universally superior.

121ba57b-2ea8-4643-914a-04d932cf7d14.takeaway: There are several ways to structure multiple relationships. None is best for everyone.

concepts.heading: The Neurochemistry of NRE
concepts.plain: That new-love rush is brain chemistry.

concepts.heading: How NRE Affects Existing Relationships
concepts.plain: The rush can make your existing relationships seem dull by comparison. They are not.

concepts.heading: Managing Your Own NRE
concepts.plain: Keep your plans and promises with existing partners.

concepts.heading: Supporting a Partner Through NRE
concepts.plain: When your partner is in the rush with someone new, it can stir up fear. That is normal.

checks.prompt: NRE is not just a feeling. It is also…
checks.explanation: A neurochemical event. NRE is not just a feeling — it's a neurochemical event. When you connect with a new person who excites you, your brain floods with dopamine (reward and motivation), norepinephrine (alertness and excitement), and oxytocin (bonding and trust).

checks.prompt: What is the first tip for managing your own NRE?
checks.explanation: Maintain your commitments. Maintain your commitments. NRE makes it tempting to cancel plans with existing partners in favor of the new connection.

6eca69b9-4114-46d6-a9f3-76af2e02f43d.takeaway: New-relationship excitement is a chemical rush. Enjoy it, and keep your promises to existing partners.
